notes.text: The phrase **God remembered** is a common expression in the Bible that often means that God was paying special attention to certain people and was about to do something. Make sure that the way you translate this phrase does not imply that God had forgotten about Noah. or [But God did not forget]
Notice that the floodwaters did not totally recede until verse 14, so the way you translate this clause should allow for that. or [so that the water level started to go down]

A **raven** is a large, black scavenger bird that eats whatever it finds, including dead animals. If the people in your language area are not familiar with ravens, you could make a comparison to a similar bird with which they are familiar and say, “a large black bird like a …” Or you could include a footnote that explains what a raven is.

In Hebrew the word **dove** is grammatically a feminine noun (for both male and female doves), so some translations say “her feet … she returned …” here. For languages such as English that do not assign grammatical gender to nouns, it is more accurate to use **its** and **it** here, because it is not known whether this dove was male or female.
Notice that the order of the people in this list varies in the Hebrew text, perhaps depending on who is in focus in each context.

When animals were sacrificed, they were killed first, not burned alive. Consider whether or not you need to make that information explicit in your translation. or [and he killed them and burned their bodies on the altar as gifts to Yahweh to honor him]
or [When Yahweh smelled the aroma of the sacrifices, he was pleased]
Consider whether or not your language has this common expression or a similar common expression that would work well here.
or [even though everything they desire is evil]
